enumeratedValue.description: SPI Exchange Bit (XCH) controls when a SPI burst can start. Setting the XCH bit will start a SPI burst or multiple bursts. This is controlled by the SPI SS Wave Form Select (SS_CTL). Refer to XCH and SS_CTL descriptions.
Immediately starts a SPI burst when data is written in TXFIFO.
The SPI_RDY signal is a don't care.
Burst will be triggered by the falling edge of the SPI_RDY signal (edge-triggered).
Burst will be triggered by a low level of the SPI_RDY signal (level-triggered).
Channel 0 is selected. Chip Select 0 (SS0) will be asserted.
Channel 1 is selected. Chip Select 1 (SS1) will be asserted.
Channel 2 is selected. Chip Select 2 (SS2) will be asserted.
Channel 3 is selected. Chip Select 3 (SS3) will be asserted.
A SPI burst contains the 1 LSB in a word.
A SPI burst contains the 2 LSB in a word.
A SPI burst contains the 3 LSB in a word.
A SPI burst contains all 32 bits in a word.
A SPI burst contains the 1 LSB in first word and all 32 bits in second word.
A SPI burst contains the 2 LSB in first word and all 32 bits in second word.
A SPI burst contains the 31 LSB in first word and 2^7 -1 words.
In master mode - only one SPI burst will be transmitted.
In master mode - Negate Chip Select (SS) signal between SPI bursts. Multiple SPI bursts will be transmitted. The SPI transfer will automatically stop when the TXFIFO is empty.

In slave mode - an SPI burst is completed when the number of bits received in the shift register is equal to (BURST LENGTH + 1). Only the n least-significant bits (n = BURST LENGTH[4:0] + 1) of the first received word are valid. All bits subsequent to the first received word in RXFIFO are valid.

In slave mode - an SPI burst is completed by the Chip Select (SS) signal edges. (SSPOL = 0: rising edge; SSPOL = 1: falling edge) The RXFIFO is advanced whenever a Chip Select (SS) signal edge is detected or the shift register contains 32-bits of valid data.
TXFIFO contains one or more words.
Number of empty slots in TXFIFO is greater than TX_THRESHOLD.
Number of empty slots in TXFIFO is not greater than TX_THRESHOLD.
When RXTDE is set - Number of data entries in the RXFIFO is not greater than RX_THRESHOLD.
When RXTDE is set - Number of data entries in the RXFIFO is greater than RX_THRESHOLD or a DMA TAIL DMA condition exists.
When RXTDE is clear - Number of data entries in the RXFIFO is not greater than RX_THRESHOLD.
When RXTDE is clear - Number of data entries in the RXFIFO is greater than RX_THRESHOLD.
Transmitter and receiver sections internally connected for Loopback.

enumeratedValue.description: Indicates to the transmit data FIFO that the written frames contain two additional octets before the frame data. This means the actual frame begins at bit 16 of the first word written into the FIFO. This function allows putting the frame payload on a 32-bit boundary in memory, as the 14-byte Ethernet header is extended to a 16-byte header.
If an IP frame is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically. The IP header checksum field must be cleared. If a non-IP frame is transmitted the frame is not modified.
If an IP frame with a known protocol is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically into the frame. The checksum field must be cleared. The other frames are not modified.

field.name: PADREM
field.description: Enable Padding Removal For Short IP Frames

enumeratedValue.description: Any bytes following the IP payload section of the frame are removed from the frame.

field.name: IPDIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong IPv4 Header Checksum

enumeratedValue.description: Frames with wrong IPv4 header checksum are not discarded.

If an IPv4 frame is received with a mismatching header checksum, the frame is discarded. IPv6 has no header checksum and is not affected by this setting. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).

field.name: PRODIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong Protocol Checksum

enumeratedValue.description: Frames with wrong checksum are not discarded.

If a TCP/IP, UDP/IP, or ICMP/IP frame is received that has a wrong TCP, UDP, or ICMP checksum, the frame is discarded. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).

field.name: LINEDIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With MAC Layer Errors

enumeratedValue.description: Frames with errors are not discarded.
Any frame received with a CRC, length, or PHY error is automatically discarded and not forwarded to the user application interface.
Instructs the MAC to write two additional bytes in front of each frame received into the RX FIFO.
The timer stops at the current value.

The timer can be reset to zero when the given offset time is reached (offset event). The field is cleared when the offset event is reached, so no further event occurs until the field is set again. The timer offset value must be set before setting this field.
The timer is not affected and no action occurs, besides clearing OFFEN, when the offset is reached.
If OFFEN is set, the timer resets to zero when the offset setting is reached. The offset event does not cause a timer interrupt.

A period event interrupt can be generated (EIR[TS_TIMER]) and the event signal output is asserted when the timer wraps around according to the periodic setting ATPER. The timer period value must be set before setting this bit. Not all devices contain the event signal output. See the chip configuration details.
The current time is captured and can be read from the ATVR register.
The timer is active and all configuration fields in this register are relevant.

The internal timer is disabled and the externally provided timer value is used. All other fields, except CAPTURE, in this register have no effect. CAPTURE can still be used to capture the current timer value.
